info.title: HelixDB HTTP API
info.summary: Execute operation-tree and Cypher queries against HelixDB
info.description: The v2 operation-tree query contract and the Cypher execution and read-only planning contract are available on local servers and Helix Cloud gateways. Local servers have no authentication. A Helix Cloud gateway decodes `Content-Encoding: gzip` or `x-gzip` request bodies and applies its 2 MiB limit after decoding, refuses other codings with 415, and gzips responses for `Accept-Encoding: gzip`; local servers do neither. The health operations describe a local server; a gateway instead serves unauthenticated `GET /health` and `GET /readyz`, whose bodies this document does not describe. On a local server, an unknown path or method returns an empty 404 or 405; Helix Cloud gateways answer unknown paths with 403 forbidden for a database key, or 400 invalid_request without authorization.

post.description: Executes one read or write batch. request_type must match the closed read or write variant under query. Local servers accept request bodies up to 16 MiB and apply no execution deadline; a write that waits for durability still returns 408 if its WAL upload exceeds 30 seconds. Helix Cloud gateways accept request bodies up to 2 MiB after gzip decoding.

requestBody.description: Maximum body size: 16 MiB on a local HelixDB server, and 2 MiB after gzip decoding on a Helix Cloud gateway. Only Helix Cloud decodes `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

204.description: Helix Cloud completed a cache-warming read and intentionally omitted the response body.

get.description: Reports process liveness and the current database and index-runtime state. Liveness returns 200 even when ready is false.
Returns 200 when the configured database handle and index runtime are ready to serve queries. The index runtime has no not-ready state, so a server that answers returns 200.

503.description: Reserved for a process whose database is not ready; current servers do not return it.

get.description: Runs read-only checks of how this server is set up and returns each verdict: storage durability, the S3 bucket's region and round-trip time, the disk cache's device, free space and startup warm, memory headroom, vector and text index publication, and the missing indexes and unbounded scans of recent queries. Checks that do not apply to the configured storage are left out. Nothing is changed; the only outbound requests are HEADs of a key that does not exist in the bucket, an unsigned HEAD of the bucket for its region, and the EC2 or ECS metadata endpoint, each bounded by a short timeout. `helix doctor` renders this report.

200.description: Every applicable check, in report order.

checks.summary: S3 bucket is in this server's region
checks.detail: Bucket helix-data and this server are both in us-east-2.

checks.summary: The disk cache is on network block storage
checks.detail: /var/cache/helix is on nvme0n1 (Amazon Elastic Block Store). Each cache miss pays network-disk latency and draws on the volume's IOPS limit; local NVMe answers several times faster.
checks.fix: Run on an instance with local NVMe (for example the i4i, i8g, m7gd or c7gd families) and mount it at /var/cache/helix, or point HELIX_DISK_CACHE_DIR at it.

post.description: Executes the supported Cypher read/CRUD profile. The server derives read/write effects from the statement; Helix Cloud routes reads to readers and writes to the elected writer. Modifying statements execute atomically in one write transaction. X-Helix-Warm is valid only for reads; X-Helix-Await-Durable:true is valid only for writes. Local servers accept request bodies up to 16 MiB. Helix Cloud gateways accept request bodies up to 2 MiB. Local servers apply a 30-second default deadline and Helix Cloud applies the database's query time limit. The response limit is 16 MiB, and resource exhaustion returns an error instead of truncation.

value.query: MATCH (n:Person) WHERE n.age >= $age RETURN n.name AS name

200.description: Statement executed successfully, including writes without RETURN.

204.description: Helix Cloud completed a cache-warming read and intentionally omitted the response body.

400.description: Malformed or oversized body, invalid request options, a missing or disallowed Helix Cloud database header, or a classified Cypher compile/runtime error. The local 16 MiB body limit returns invalid_request_body with this status.

401.description: The Helix Cloud API key is invalid. Gateway errors use the native {error,msg} envelope.

402.description: Helix Cloud query processing is disabled because the tenant has exhausted its credit.

403.description: The Helix Cloud API key cannot run this statement; a read-only key can read and explain but not write.

404.description: The statement reached a missing index.

408.description: The statement exceeded its deadline: 30 seconds on a local server (`query_deadline_exceeded`), or the Helix Cloud query time limit (`query_timeout`). A write that waits for durability also returns 408, once applied, if its WAL upload exceeds 30 seconds. A write may have committed: read the state back before resending.

409.description: A storage transaction conflict (`transaction_conflict`, `retryable: true`) or a conflict with the database's state, such as `unique_constraint_violation` (`retryable: false`).

413.description: The Helix Cloud gateway rejected a request body larger than 2 MiB before parsing it, with payload_too_large.

415.description: A Helix Cloud gateway refused a Content-Encoding other than gzip or identity (`unsupported_content_encoding`).

Accept-Encoding.description: The content coding the gateway accepts.

429.description: Branch on `error`: a Cypher resource limit (`resource_limit`; inspect details.detail) fails again when resent unchanged and carries no retryable; a Helix Cloud rate limit (`rate_limited`) carries Retry-After; `index_backpressure` carries `retryable: true` and committed nothing.

500.description: Internal planner, storage, execution-control, or serialization failure.

503.description: Writer required, server access mode unavailable, or uncertain write commit. A local uncertain outcome carries retryable:false; Helix Cloud reports one as write_outcome_unknown with retryable:false, like native queries.

post.description: Translates one SQL statement to the supported Cypher profile and executes it exactly like POST /v2/cypher: the same read/write routing, request headers, authentication, results, lossless values, and error body. SELECT becomes MATCH and RETURN, INSERT becomes CREATE, UPDATE becomes SET, and DELETE and TRUNCATE delete. Tables map to node labels and joins to relationships by syntax alone; `mappings` renames tables and join columns. `?` placeholders bind to `parameters` given as a list, in written order; `:name`, `$name` and `@name` bind to an object. Translation errors use the Cypher error body with a span in the SQL text. Helix Cloud routes reads to readers and writes to the elected writer. Local servers accept request bodies up to 16 MiB. Helix Cloud gateways accept request bodies up to 2 MiB. Local servers apply a 30-second default deadline and Helix Cloud applies the database's query time limit. The response limit is 16 MiB, and resource exhaustion returns an error instead of truncation.

value.query: SELECT p.name, m.title FROM Person p JOIN ACTED_IN r ON r.person_id = p.id JOIN Movie m ON m.id = r.movie_id WHERE p.born > ?

bearerAuth.description: Helix Cloud cluster API key. Local servers have no authentication and ignore it.

DatabaseId.name: X-Helix-Database-Id
DatabaseId.description: Database identifier shown in Helix Cloud connection details. Required by the GA shared gateway, not needed by a standalone local server, and not allowed by a database-specific cluster-mode gateway. The legacy X-Helix-Tenant-Id alias is also accepted in GA mode.

WarmOnly.name: X-Helix-Warm
WarmOnly.description: Warm read execution state. Valid only for read requests.

RequireWriter.name: X-Helix-Require-Writer
RequireWriter.description: Require the writer. A local server that is not a writer rejects the request with 503 `writer_mode_required`; a Helix Cloud gateway routes the request to the writer instead of a reader.

AwaitDurable.name: X-Helix-Await-Durable
AwaitDurable.description: Omit it or send true, on write requests only, and success means the write is durable. Send false to acknowledge a write once it is applied on the writer, before its WAL upload; a crash before that upload loses it. A Helix Cloud gateway rejects false on a write with 400 `invalid_request`.

BadRequest.description: Invalid JSON, query plan, vector input, request option, or Helix Cloud authentication header.

Unauthorized.description: The Helix Cloud API key is invalid.

PaymentRequired.description: Helix Cloud query processing is disabled because the tenant has exhausted its credit.

Forbidden.description: The Helix Cloud API key does not have permission to execute the query.

NotFound.description: The query named a node, edge, index or index operation that does not exist.

RequestTimeout.description: The query exceeded a deadline: `query_deadline_exceeded` from the engine, or `query_timeout` from a Helix Cloud wall-clock limit. A local server applies no execution deadline to /v2/query, but a write that waits for durability returns 408, once applied, if its WAL upload exceeds 30 seconds. A write may have committed: read the state back before resending.

Conflict.description: A conflict. `transaction_conflict` (`retryable: true`) lost to concurrent work and can be retried; a conflict with the database's state, such as `unique_constraint_violation` (`retryable: false`), committed nothing and fails again when resent.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The Helix Cloud gateway rejected a request body larger than 2 MiB before query parsing.

example.msg: request body exceeds the maximum allowed size

UnsupportedContentEncoding.description: The Helix Cloud gateway refused a Content-Encoding other than gzip or identity.

Accept-Encoding.description: The content coding the gateway accepts.

example.msg: Content-Encoding must be gzip or identity

RateLimited.description: Branch on `error`. `rate_limited`: the Helix Cloud gateway rate limit was exceeded; wait for Retry-After. `query_memory_limit_exceeded`: the query exceeded its memory budget; it fails again when resent unchanged and carries no retryable. `index_backpressure` (`retryable: true`): the database rejected a write because a vector or text index already retains its maximum unpublished work, or a whole-index strong search whose answer lies behind more than 800 unpublished changes (eventual and prefiltered searches are never rejected this way), or a strong text search that would analyze more unpublished text in its partition than its bound allows (512 MiB of analysis by default), or a strong vector search that would score more unpublished vector work than its bound allows (by default the index's retained-byte limit, which writes reach first). Eventual searches are never rejected for unpublished text or vector work. Backpressure rejects the whole request (writes before commit).

Retry-After.description: Delay before retrying, when supplied by the gateway.

InternalError.description: An internal query, storage, or serialization failure occurred.

Unavailable.description: A required writer or ready database is unavailable, or, with `retryable: false`, a write's commit outcome is unknown.

query_name.description: Optional diagnostic name. It does not create a stored endpoint.

search_consistency.description: Visibility of committed vector/text changes the index worker has not published yet. `strong` searches every committed change; `eventual` overlays a bounded budget of unpublished changes per search and may omit the rest until publication.

query_name.description: Optional diagnostic name. It does not create a stored endpoint.

search_consistency.description: Write batches always search strongly and see their own uncommitted changes.

BatchCondition.description: Externally tagged condition for a conditional batch entry.

OperationTree.description: One externally tagged, snake_case HelixDB AstNode operation. Source operations start a traversal; subsequent operations contain their predecessor under input. Use a typed HelixDB SDK or the query documentation to construct this recursive tree.

QueryParameterValue.description: JSON-compatible runtime parameter. Datetimes are RFC 3339 strings when declared as date_time. Raw bytes cannot be represented on the JSON route. Integer and floating-point JSON numbers are accepted for f32 and f64 declarations and converted to the declared type. Values must be finite; f32 values must fit within its finite range.

QueryParameterTypes.description: When present, keys must exactly match parameters. Typed and untyped parameters cannot be mixed. Floating-point declarations accept integer or floating-point JSON numbers and convert them to the declared f32 or f64 type.

QueryResponse.description: Returned variables keyed by the names listed in the batch returns array.

QueryError.description: Stable error envelope returned by local servers and Helix Cloud gateways.

retryable.description: Present only when the code's failure class settles it: true for a retryable conflict (409) and `index_backpressure` (429), which committed nothing; false for a conflict with the database's state (409), such as `unique_constraint_violation`, and for an unknown write outcome (503). Absence is not permission to retry.

blocked_index_entity_count.description: Nodes and edges whose queued vector or text index work the index worker holds back: either it can never fit a publication under the current limits, typically after the limits were lowered, or applying it fails the same way every time, for example on damaged index data. Only the count: the writer logs an error naming each one when it is held back. Always 0 on a reader. Rebuilt after a restart as publication reaches them again.

uptime_secs.description: Seconds since the server opened its database.

status.description: `warn`: works but costs performance or money. `fail`: risks losing data. `skip`: the check could not run; `detail` says why.

detail.description: What was observed, or why the check was skipped. May span several lines.

fix.description: What to change; present only for `warn` and `fail`. May contain `<instance>`, which a client that knows the instance's name substitutes.

value.description: Signed 64-bit decimal integer. Use this envelope outside the JavaScript safe integer range to avoid precision loss.

oneOf.description: Finite JSON number. Signed integers outside ±9007199254740991 should use the integer envelope. Fractional or exponent-form values retain floating-point semantics.

CypherParameterValue.description: Scalar, list, or map parameter. Graph elements cannot be supplied as parameters. Escape a map whose $type is a string with the map envelope. Integer input must fit signed 64-bit range.

oneOf.description: Finite JSON number. Signed integers outside ±9007199254740991 should use the integer envelope. Fractional or exponent-form values retain floating-point semantics.

CypherValue.description: Lossless recursive result value. Escape literal maps containing $type with the map envelope. Graph IDs are unsigned decimal strings; id() instead uses checked signed conversion.

CypherId.description: Unsigned 64-bit graph identifier, 0 through 18446744073709551615, encoded as a decimal string. Never convert implicitly to a JavaScript number.

properties.description: User properties only; internal Helix metadata is omitted.

CypherPath.description: Ordered walk with exactly one more node than relationship. Relationship endpoints retain their stored direction, including when traversed backwards.

CypherRequest.description: Unknown fields are rejected with invalid_query_json, as is a body nested more than 127 levels deep.

query.description: One statement in the supported Cypher profile; empty or unsupported statements return a classified query error.

CypherResponse.description: Column order defines each row. Every row has exactly columns.length cells. Duplicates are preserved unless the query removes them. Row order is guaranteed only by ORDER BY. A successful statement without RETURN has empty columns and rows. Planner diagnostics are returned separately by the explain operation.

detail.description: The specific condition within the category, in lower snake case, such as `undefined_variable` or `memory_limit`.

span.description: Optional half-open source span [start,end), measured in UTF-8 bytes; null when unavailable.

error.description: Machine-readable lower snake case code: a Cypher category, such as `syntax_error` or `resource_limit`, or a native transport or storage error code.

retryable.description: Present only on native-envelope bodies, which have no details, when the code's failure class settles it: true for `transaction_conflict`, `request_read_view_changed`, `stale_index_generation` and `index_backpressure`; false for a conflict with the database's state, such as `unique_constraint_violation`, and for an uncertain commit outcome. Do not retry a modifying statement automatically on false.

CypherError.description: Query errors include details and never retryable. Request, storage, and transaction errors retain the native envelope without details, including its optional retryable. An uncertain commit returns retryable:false; a missing retryable is not permission to retry.

logical.description: Resolved frontend-independent logical operator; detailed planner representation may evolve.

contract.description: Derived input/output slots, effects, references, correlation, multiplicity, and optimization boundaries.

graph.description: Selected access steps and sources, estimated_rows_per_input, and cartesian_products for MATCH; null for other operators.

batch_consumer.description: Selected downstream batch consumer, or null when the selected plan materializes the relation.

planner.description: Selected costs, cardinality/cost estimates, memo/rule work, and guardrail exhaustion. Estimates do not limit results.

CypherExplanation.description: Read-only planning response. Explaining a modifying statement does not execute it. Planner internals may evolve independently of the stable columns/rows execution response.

SqlRequest.description: Unknown fields are rejected with invalid_query_json, as is a body nested more than 127 levels deep.

query.description: One SQL statement: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE. Statements outside the translation return a classified query error.

parameters.description: Values for `?` placeholders as a list in written order (the first binds `$1`), or named values for `:name` and `$name` placeholders.

SqlMappings.description: How SQL names map onto the graph; keys match case-insensitively.

tables.description: Table name to node label, or to relationship type for the middle table of a join.

join_columns.description: `table.column` of a join condition to relationship type; the table is the join's left table.
